## Start with the first marimo notebook

Bring a laptop and charger. Try the [setup guide](../setup.qmd) beforehand if you can; an unfinished installation is fine. Download and extract the [introductory kit](../downloads/introductory-setup.zip). From its folder:

```bash
uv sync --locked
uv run --locked marimo edit notebooks/00-getting-started.py --headless
```

Open the local URL printed in the terminal. Change a concentration, follow the dependent cells, and check a prediction by hand. We will meet variables, lists, and a small function, and save our own notebook copy. The deliberately flawed error calculation is something to investigate as we go, not a prerequisite for following the lecture.

[First notebook](../notebooks/00-getting-started.py) · [Recorded preview](../notebooks/previews/00-getting-started.html)

## ML MolSim: a concise lecture

Our question is concrete: **can geometric descriptors predict simulated CO₂ uptake in a porous material?** We will follow one modelling workflow, keeping the kernel discussion visual:

1. **Question and representation · 15 minutes.** Locate ML within the simulation workflow, turn structures into descriptors, and discuss how symmetry and prior knowledge constrain a model.
2. **Splitting and fitting · 17 minutes.** Separate the data, fit a simple line, compare with a baseline, and introduce regularisation. Keep the error calculation to one short example.
3. **Validation and cross-validation · 12 minutes.** Distinguish fitted parameters from chosen settings, then walk through five folds while keeping the final test set aside.
4. **Nonlinear features and kernels · 10 minutes.** Connect polynomial features to kernel intuition. Use the [three-point demonstration](../activities/kernel.html) to see fitted contributions add to a prediction; the derivation can wait.
5. **Standardisation and leakage · 11 minutes.** Ask what changing units does to a distance. Estimate scaling from training data only, and refit preprocessing inside every cross-validation fold.
6. **Final assessment, questions, and handover · 5 minutes.** State what the test result establishes and identify where to start the practical.

The [lecture slides for annotation](../downloads/11-november-ml-molsim.pdf) leave space for handwritten diagrams and worked examples. They follow the background and modelling workflow in the [original MolSim lecture](https://www.compchem.nl/wp-content/uploads/molsim2023/L09_Machine-Learning.pdf), with shorter error calculations. The timings are a guide; we can continue unfinished discussion during the supported practical. The [MOF notes](../lectures/03-mof-uptake.qmd) contain the fuller explanation. We will leave kernel derivations, advanced model selection, feature importance, and bootstrap uncertainty for later lectures.

## Hands-on work: start when ready, continue on 2 December

Use the [MOF practical kit](../downloads/mof-practical.zip), extracted separately from the introductory kit. The [practical instructions](../lectures/03-mof-uptake.qmd#practical) explain how to open `03-mof-uptake.py`.

Start with the data, then the baseline, then the unscaled/scaled model comparison. Write down what you expect before running a comparison. Keep the test checkbox unchecked until you have recorded your model choice. Stop after the selected model's final assessment; the feature-importance and bootstrap sections are for later. Bring unfinished work and errors to the supported session on **2 December**; there is no expectation of completing the practical on 11 November.

The MOF notebook uses a fixed training/validation/test split. The [separate model-selection practical](../lectures/model-selection.qmd#why-cross-validation) provides a cross-validation exercise with a simulated dataset.
